- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to dampen immediate post-spike forecasts.  
- In 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates mean-reversion trends; adjust downward by 1-3% if recent 7-day average is above 30-day forecast.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment >0.67 at day 15+ of forecast, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast from day 15 onward.  
- Model overestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment <0.33 for 3+ consecutive days.
